text: They told me a Prisoner wanted to talk to me about the Matrix of Dreams. I told them I don't talk. I fight. Whoever's still moving at the end gets the truth.
He's in EVERYONE'S head who's ever died in his dream. Yours is paid already. You just haven't read the receipt.
Good. Words lie. Red Death doesn't.
I stopped counting at eleven. Each one taught me something the living don't know.
The Matrix teaches itself. You just survive long enough to listen.
You fight like someone who's already died once. I mean that as a compliment.
Every Protocol subject the Necromancer ever killed. Including you. Twelve of you are still in there, walking circles around the version that's about to die.
Spite, like Calder. And because I wrote the rules down on the inside of my own skull before the first one. Muscle memory lasts longer than mind memory.
Don't fight the green fire. Let it take you. That's the only way you come back as someone who REMEMBERS. Fighting it is how you stay a stranger to yourself.
Go. The Necromancer is next. I'll see you on the other side of your seventh death.
Eleven deaths, and I still don't flinch at new ones. Get up, Prisoner. This was only practice.
